key_insight: Neuronally-enriched extracellular vesicle synaptopodin in blood is a prognostic marker of disability progression and brain integrity decline in progressive multiple sclerosis, especially SPMS.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this blood-based biomarker could help identify progressive MS patients at higher risk of worsening and improve monitoring beyond neurofilament light chain alone.
method: Measured synaptopodin in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles from blood
Tested associations in two cohorts: SPRINT-MS (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268)
Linked baseline and longitudinal biomarker levels to disability progression and MRI outcomes
evidence_signal: Across two cohorts, higher baseline NEV synaptopodin was associated with lower risk of confirmed disability progression and stronger MRI preservation signals, with replication in the validation cohort and added predictive value over NfL in SPMS.
watch_item: This is an observational biomarker study, so clinical utility will depend on external validation, assay standardization, and clear thresholds for use in practice.
paper_title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis
